slides.say: A B C D is a rhombus. Given: B D is ten centimeters, and angle A B D is sixty degrees. What is the area of the rhombus, in square centimeters?
at: A B C D is a rhombus

slides.say: We learned two formulas for the area of a rhombus. A rhombus is a parallelogram with all its sides equal, so one formula is side times the height to that side. The other is the two diagonals multiplied, over two. That one works for any quadrilateral whose diagonals are perpendicular. [short pause] A diagonal is given here, so we'll start with the diagonal formula.
[short pause] In a rhombus, the diagonals cut each other in half. So let's draw the other diagonal, from A to C. It cuts B D into five and five.
at: It cuts B D into five and five

slides.say: The diagonals of a rhombus are also perpendicular, so the angle at O is ninety. That makes a special triangle, A B O. It's a right triangle with a sixty-degree angle, so it's a gold triangle, thirty, sixty, ninety.
In a gold triangle the sides have a fixed ratio. Five is across from the thirty-degree angle, so it's the short leg. To get the long leg, we multiply by root three. So A O is five root three.
at: So A O is five root three

slides.say: The diagonals cut each other in half, so the bottom part, O C, is five root three too. The whole diagonal A C is five root three plus five root three, which is ten root three.
Now the formula, for the whole rhombus. The diagonals multiplied, over two, is ten times ten root three, over two.
Ten over two is five, and five times ten root three is fifty root three. Choice number two is our answer.
at: and five times ten root three
Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Once you've found all the inner pieces, you can add up the area in other ways too. Some students take the gold triangle, base five and height five root three, and multiply its area by four, because the rhombus is made of four of these triangles.
at: Once you've found all the inner pieces
Some students take the gold triangle

slides.say: Some take the top triangle, B D A. Its base is B D, ten, and its height is A O, five root three. The bottom triangle, B D C, is the same, so we take it twice.
at: The bottom triangle, B D C

slides.say: And some take the triangle on the right, A D C. Its base is A C, ten root three, and its height is O D, five. The left triangle is the same, so again we take it twice. These all use rules we know, so pick whichever you see first.
at: And some take the triangle on
The left triangle is the same
so again we take it twice

slides.say: [pause] And one more way, an insight. Some students notice the sixty degrees and say, wait, that's a hint.
In a rhombus all the sides are equal, so A B equals A D. That makes triangle A B D isosceles, and angle A D B is sixty too.
at: so A B equals A D

slides.say: Sixty plus sixty is one hundred twenty, so the top angle is sixty as well. The triangle is equilateral. It's worth remembering that an isosceles triangle with a sixty-degree angle is always equilateral. B D is ten, so A B and A D are ten.
at: so the top angle is sixty as well

slides.say: All the sides of a rhombus are equal, so D C and B C are ten too. So the rhombus is two equilateral triangles.
at: so D C and B C are ten too
So the rhombus is two equilateral

slides.say: The area of one equilateral triangle is the side squared, times root three, over four. The side is ten, and ten squared is a hundred. So one triangle is a hundred root three, over four.
The rhombus is two of these triangles, so we take it twice. That's two hundred root three, over four, which is fifty root three. Choice number two.
at: fifty root three. Choice number two

slides.say: And one more link to the triangles topic. Angle A B C is sixty plus sixty, one hundred twenty. So triangle A B C is the thirty, thirty, one hundred twenty triangle with sides ten and ten, and its long side, A C, is ten root three straight away. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: Angle A B C is sixty plus sixty
